name: B10-0407/2026 (ECR) – Deteriorating situation of media freedom and freedom of expression in Hong Kong following the recent arrest of bookseller Leticia Wong and the convictions of Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the deteriorating situation of media freedom and freedom of expression in Hong Kong following the recent arrest of bookseller Leticia Wong and the convictions of Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung
part_text:
The European Parliament is not changing any law here. It is stating its opinion and making requests. It condemns what it calls the systematic destruction of media freedom and free speech in Hong Kong under the 2020 National Security Law and a 2024 security ordinance. It names four people: bookseller Leticia Wong, recently arrested; Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan, convicted; and Jimmy Lai, sentenced to 20 years. It asks Hong Kong to release them and asks the European Union to sanction officials responsible.

- No law changes. The Parliament asks the European Union to sanction Hong Kong and Chinese officials it holds responsible.
- It affects Hong Kong journalists, publishers and activists, including the four named people.
- Next, the resolution goes to the European Commission, the Council, China and Hong Kong.
